rationale: This is the archived KnowledgeEffortVsEnterpriseMultiple with two parameter-level substitutions (pooled→industry ranks, 1-year flow→5-year sum) and no new economic channel, so it is a cosmetic variant of an already-evaluated signal rather than a substantively different test.

The change addresses a genuine mechanical defect in the archived signal — R&D/sales rising because sales collapse — by deflating the incremental R&D dollar with predetermined lagged assets, which is an economically motivated repair rather than a relabeling, and the expression matches the stated hypothesis.

The COALESCE(xrd,0) imputation makes VOL identically zero for firms that never report R&D, so NEG(VOL) awards them the maximum stability score and the long leg fills with cheap non-innovators — the exact value traps the hypothesis claims to exclude.

Internally consistent and coherently motivated by the gen-0 sign evidence, but it is close to an additive stack of two documented effects (EBITDA/EV value and the goodwill/acquired-intangible underperformance anomaly), and the inference that a multiplicative interaction's negative alpha implies a negative standalone intan/at loading is loose.

Replacing the failed productivity level with a five-year trend is a defensible change in economic content and the sign logic is consistent, though the profitability-trend leg partly rediscovers the published fundamental-trend/profitability-change anomaly and 5-point annual trends are noisy.

This is a kitchen-sink stack of three channels already tested in the archive, with arbitrary implicit weights from the nested SUMRANK (1/2 on cheapness, 1/4 each on the intangible legs), so any result would be uninterpretable and unattributable to a specific mechanism.
